idiom_name: Rack middleware: initialize(app) / call(env), stacked with Rack::Builder#use
implementation_notes: Rack fixes the contract that makes the pattern trivial: a middleware is any object whose call(env) returns [status, headers, body], holding the downstream application in its constructor, and Rack::Builder#use stacks middlewares in the declared order - env is the Context and returning a response without calling @app.call(env) vetoes the rest of the stack. The classic Interceptor/Dispatcher classes are replaced by the builder plus the application-callable protocol, so nothing has to be hand-built for HTTP; inside Rails the same concern can be expressed as filter callbacks (before_action/around_action) declared on the controller, which is the framework-level rather than the stack-level form. A hand-written dispatcher is only justified for non-Rack events (background jobs, custom event buses).
code_sketch:
class TimingMiddleware
  def initialize(app); @app = app; end   # registered once

  def call(env)
    t0 = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    status, headers, body = @app.call(env)          # downstream chain
    headers['x-runtime'] = ((Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t0) * 1000).round.to_s
    [status, headers, body]
  end
end
pitfalls: The Rack body must be consumed or closed properly (close must be called at least once); a middleware that calls body.each directly or replaces the body without closing the original leaks resources and breaks streaming responses.
Middleware instances are created once and shared across threads (Puma, Sidekiq): instance state must be immutable or synchronised - per-request data belongs in env.
Reading the request body in middleware consumes rack.input unless it is rewindable: buffer it and reassign env['rack.input'], or downstream parsers see an empty body.
Constant autoloading: referencing application constants while middleware is constructed during boot can raise NameError instead of autoloading - eager-load or keep middleware self-contained.
